find: On the night of 30 June 1934, SS and Gestapo units murdered Röhm and around 85 SA leaders in the so-called Night of the Long Knives.
replace: Between 30 June and 2 July 1934, SS and Gestapo units murdered at least 85 people in the so-called Night of the Long Knives. Only about half of the named victims were SA men, and Röhm himself was shot in a Munich prison on 1 July.
note: F10: 85 is the documented total for the whole purge, of whom only about 50 were SA; Roehm was shot on 1 July 1934.

expect: 30 June 1934 — Ernst Röhm and around 85 SA leaders killed.
value: 30 June to 2 July 1934 — at least 85 people killed, including the SA leader Ernst Röhm.

find: The Reich Mothers’ Cross, introduced in 1933, awarded medals
replace: The Reich Mothers’ Cross, introduced in December 1938, awarded medals

expect: Medal awarded from 1933 for having four (bronze), six (silver) or eight or more (gold) children.
value: Medal introduced in December 1938 for having four (bronze), six (silver) or eight or more (gold) children.

find: Field Marshal Paulus surrendered on 2 February 1943 with approximately 91,000 surviving troops (from an original force of over 300,000).
replace: Field Marshal Paulus surrendered on 31 January 1943 and the last German troops gave in on 2 February. About 91,000 men went into captivity from an original force of over 300,000.
note: F28: Paulus surrendered on 31 January 1943; the northern pocket held out until 2 February.

find: Approximately 5,000 people were subsequently arrested and around 200 executed, including von Stauffenberg himself

note: F29: the Gestapo arrested more than 7,000 people after the plot and 4,980 were executed; 5,000 is the execution figure, not the arrest figure.

value: Von Stauffenberg's bomb exploded at Hitler's HQ but Hitler survived; over 7,000 people were arrested and nearly 5,000 executed.
